question: Can InfRing preserve native agent-framework capabilities through the Agent Runtime socket?

proof_accounting_rule.note: Agent Runtime harness success proves InfRing can mediate and govern external frameworks. It does not by itself prove native InfRing intelligence or native workflow usefulness.

scoring_dimensions.description: The framework can use prior turns or supplied context without starting cold.
The framework exposes useful activity/decision/tool status, not only final answer text.
Mutating actions are mediated through approval and can resume after a decision.
Read/write/artifact behavior is observable, bounded, and receipt-backed.
The selected model/provider intent is discoverable and respected.
Auth/quota/runtime failures become explicit diagnostics rather than silent hangs.
InfRing socket behavior preserves the framework capability that works natively.

hard_rules: Dry-run is default; live agent execution requires explicit opt-in.
Native and InfRing runs must use a disposable harness workspace unless a task explicitly declares otherwise.
Mutating tasks must declare approval expectations.
Shell display behavior may be observed, but Shell must not own scoring or task definitions.
Adapters may translate private framework schemas, but must not become policy owners.
